nodes.summary: Let $\pi_{12}$ be a probability measure on $X_1 \times X_2$ and $\pi_{23}$ a probability measure on $X_2 \times X_3$ such that the second marginal of $\pi_{12}$ equals the first marginal of $\pi_{23}$. If $X_3$ is a standard Borel space, there is a probability measure $\pi$ on $(X_1 \times X_2) \times X_3$ whose marginal on $X_1 \times X_2$ is $\pi_{12}$ and whose marginal on $X_2 \times X_3$ is $\pi_{23}$.

nodes.summary: For a probability measure $\mu$, the image of $\mu$ under the diagonal map $x \mapsto (x, x)$ is a coupling of $\mu$ with itself: the deterministic coupling given by the identity map.

nodes.summary: If $\pi$ is a coupling of $\mu$ and $\nu$, its image under $(y, z) \mapsto (z, y)$ is a coupling of $\nu$ and $\mu$.

On a second-countable pseudo-extended metric space whose σ-algebra contains the open sets, $W_p(\mu, 
u) = W_p(
u, \mu)$ for every real $p$ and all probability measures $\mu,

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be an extended metric space with its Borel σ-algebra. For $p > 0$ and $x, y \in X$, $W_p(\delta_x, \delta_y) = d(x, y)$. The only coupling of two Dirac masses is $\delta_{(x, y)}$; here it is enough that every coupling is concentrated on $\{(x, y)\}$.
